manifest.title: MariaDB Server
manifest.author: MariaDB Foundation
manifest.description:
## About

A standalone MariaDB 11.8 server for clients outside of Cloudron, with a web panel to manage roles and databases.

* Connections are TLS 1.3 only, using the app domain's certificate
* Passwords are generated by the panel. Instead, a login can use Cloudron app passwords created in the user's profile
* Remote access is blocked until a network is added to the allowlist
* Each role only gets access to its own databases
* Sign in with Cloudron. Admins manage roles, databases and allowed networks. Roles are owned by Cloudron users and groups, every owner has an own login
* Users can create, download and restore snapshots of their databases
* Users can upload SQL dumps from mariadb-dump or mysqldump and import them into their databases
* Users can turn on mails about failed snapshots, restores and imports
* Admins can change selected MariaDB settings such as max_connections and innodb_buffer_pool_size
* Backups are logical dumps taken by Cloudron's backup, snapshots stay on the server and are not part of them
manifest.tagline: Standalone MariaDB server reachable from external hosts

create-admin-group.message: Set admins: add Cloudron usernames to MARIADB_ADMINS in /app/data/env.sh, or add users to a Cloudron group named mariadb-admins. Restart the app after editing env.sh.

MARIADB_PORT.title: MariaDB Port
MARIADB_PORT.description: Port for MariaDB client connections (TLS only)

manifest.changelog:
* Initial version with MariaDB 11.8.6
* Remote access over TLS 1.3, blocked until a network is added to the allowlist
* Admin panel with Cloudron login: roles, databases, allowed networks, server settings, audit log
* Roles are owned by Cloudron users and groups. Every owner has an own login, it is locked when the user is no longer an owner
* Logins can use Cloudron app passwords instead of a generated password
* Owners can create databases up to a limit set by the admin
* Snapshots on demand and on a schedule, download as .sql.zst or .sql, restore into a staging database that is swapped in
* Import of uploaded SQL dumps (plain, gzip or zstd) with SHA-256 checks
* Live progress for snapshots, restores and imports
* Opt-in mails about failed snapshots, restores and imports
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Remote connections are blocked until you allow a network.

1. Make yourself an admin: set `MARIADB_ADMINS="<your username>"` in `/app/data/env.sh` and restart the app, or add yourself to a Cloudron group named `mariadb-admins`.
2. Open the app, sign in, and go to **Admin**.
3. Add the IP address of your client server under **Admin > Network**.
4. Create a role under **Admin > Roles** and choose its owners (Cloudron users and groups).
5. Each owner signs in, opens the role settings (gear icon) on **My databases** and creates an own password. It is shown once and not stored.
6. Connect with TLS verification, using your login `<role>.<username>`:
   `mariadb --host=$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN --port=<port> --user=<role>.<username> --password --ssl-verify-server-cert <database>`
   With the MySQL client use `--ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY`. If your system has no Let's Encrypt root certificate, download [isrgrootx1.pem](https://letsencrypt.org/certs/isrgrootx1.pem) and pass it with `--ssl-ca`.

manifest.changelog:
* Audit log has a search, a filter by type and pages
* Admin groups are set with MARIADB_ADMIN_GROUP in /app/data/env.sh, one or more groups separated by commas. New installs have no admin group, existing installs keep mariadb-admins
* Name fields explain the allowed characters and why a name is not accepted, capitals become lowercase
* Admin > Server shows the default value of each empty setting
* New app icon with the official MariaDB logo
* Fixed the upload form layout on phones and the account tooltip in the top bar
